en.title: Titles and forms of address
en.summary: Titles and names are the main forms of address in English.

paragraphs: Forms of address are the words we use to speak to a person: names, titles and family words. The choice shows how well we know the person, how old they are and how formal the situation is. English is generally less formal than many other languages.

Use Mr, Ms, Mrs, Miss or Dr with a surname. Among friends, and in most workplaces, people use first names. Sir and madam are used in service situations. Ms does not show whether a woman is married, so it is the safest choice. A title is never used alone with a first name, so we do not say Mr John.

paragraphs: The older or higher-ranking person often invites the change: Please call me Anna. Do not change to first names before this unless the other person does. In many offices it happens at the first meeting.
A formal letter begins Dear Mr Brown or Dear Sir or Madam. A friendly email can begin Hi Anna. We end formally with Yours sincerely or Yours faithfully, and informally with Best wishes or Cheers.

items: Wrong: **Mr John, please come in.** Right: **Mr Brown, please come in.**
Wrong: **Hey, you!** (to a customer) Right: **Excuse me, sir.**
Wrong: **Mrs Clark** (to an unknown woman) Right: **Ms Clark**

ro.title: Titluri și forme de adresare
ro.summary: În limba română folosim titluri de politețe și nume pentru a vorbi respectuos cu alte persoane.

paragraphs: Când vorbim cu o persoană, folosim cuvinte speciale numite formule de adresare. Acestea pot fi nume, titluri de politețe sau termeni de rudenie. Formulele de adresare arată respectul nostru față de cealaltă persoană.

Folosim titlurile „domnul” și „doamna” împreună cu numele de familie. Când vorbim direct cu un bărbat, spunem „domnule”, iar când vorbim cu o femeie, spunem „doamnă”. Cu prietenii și în familie folosim de obicei prenumele.
